### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

35.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Calling navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: { mandatory: { chromeMediaSource: 'desktop', chromeMediaSourceId: source.id } } }) with a valid source.id obtained from desktopCapturer.getSources should return a MediaStream containing the audio track from the specified window or screen, without crashing the renderer process.

Alternatively, navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({ audio: true, video: false }) should ideally either return a stream with system/loopback audio or prompt the user with a picker that allows audio sharing, rather than throwing NotSupportedError

### Actual Behavior

1. getUserMedia + chromeMediaSourceId: The renderer process terminates instantly upon calling await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(...) with the desktop audio constraints. The DevTools disconnect, and the terminal running Electron often shows:
[21192:0330/145830.258:ERROR:bad_message.cc(29)] Terminating renderer for bad IPC message, reason 263
Error 263 corresponds to BadMessageReason::DESKTOP_CAPTURER_INVALID_OR_UNKNOWN_ID). This happens for all tested window sources (Chrome, Spotify, VLC, etc.) and "Entire Screen" sources.

2. getDisplayMedia({ audio: true }): Calling await navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({ audio: true, video: false }) immediately throws a NotSupportedError: Not supported, indicating desktop audio capture via this API is unavailable in this environment.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Troubleshooting Steps & Outcomes:

Initial Approach (getUserMedia + chromeMediaSourceId in Preload):

Attempt: Tried requiring desktopCapturer directly in preload.js and exposing getSources via contextBridge. Then calling getUserMedia with the obtained chromeMediaSourceId in audio.js.

Outcome: Failed. The require('electron') call in preload.js did not include desktopCapturer on your system, even with stable Electron versions and clean installs. The API wasn't exposed.

IPC for getSources + getUserMedia in Renderer:

Attempt: Moved desktopCapturer.getSources logic to main.js. Exposed an IPC function (electronAPI.getSources) via preload.js that called the Main process handler using ipcRenderer.invoke. The Renderer (audio.js) successfully received the list of sources via this IPC call. Then, audio.js called getUserMedia with the chromeMediaSourceId from the received list.

Outcome: Failed. While fetching the source list worked, the getUserMedia call in the Renderer crashed the renderer process instantly with Error 263 (DESKTOP_CAPTURER_INVALID_OR_UNKNOWN_ID) in the terminal. This happened for all source types (windows and screens).

Debugging getUserMedia Crash:

Attempt: Verified the source.id being passed was correct (string, matched the list). Ruled out simple timing issues by confirming the crash was immediate. Confirmed crash happens even when the target window is active and visible.

Outcome: Confirmed the parameters were correct, but the crash persisted, pointing to an internal Electron/Chromium issue handling that specific API call with desktop source IDs.

Session Permission Handlers:

Attempt: Added session.setPermissionCheckHandler and session.setPermissionRequestHandler in main.js to explicitly allow the 'media' permission, in case newer Electron versions required it for internal desktop capture checks.

Outcome: Failed. The renderer still crashed with Error 263 when getUserMedia was called.

Alternative API: getDisplayMedia({ audio: true }):

Attempt: Implemented a separate function calling navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({ audio: true, video: false }) in the Renderer (with enableBlinkFeatures: 'GetDisplayMedia' possibly set in Main).

Outcome: Failed. The API call immediately threw a NotSupportedError: Not supported, indicating the environment doesn't support desktop audio capture via this method.

Environmental Checks:

Attempt: Tested different Electron versions , performed clean installs (rm -rf node_modules && npm install), temporarily disabled antivirus.

Outcome: No change. The issues persisted across versions and with antivirus off, strongly suggesting an environment-specific incompatibility or bug rather than a project setup or temporary glitch. Minimal test cases also failed similarly on your machine.

Workaround: Virtual Audio Cable:

Attempt: Refactored the app to ignore desktopCapturer. Instead, listed audio input devices using navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices (via preload). The user selects an input (like "CABLE Output"). The app calls getUserMedia using the selected deviceId. Requires users to manually route application audio to the virtual cable outside the app.

Outcome: Partially Successful. The app no longer crashes. It successfully lists audio input devices (including the virtual cable) and captures audio from the selected device using getUserMedia({ audio: { deviceId: ... } }). However, this does not meet the original requirement of capturing and routing per-application audio, as it only captures the single, mixed stream coming out of the virtual cable.
items.title: Renderer Crashes (Error 263) using getUserMedia with chromeMediaSourceId for Desktop Audio Capture on Windows 11 with bad ipc
